message.content:
1. Use 384‑well MaxiSorp plates (Nunc) and coat each well with the capture antibody α‑Syn (BD Biosciences, catalog 610787) diluted 1 : 500 in coating buffer (0.05 M NaHCO₃, 0.2 % NaN₃, pH 9.6). Incubate the plates overnight at 4 °C.  

2. Wash the plates three times with PBS containing 0.05 % Tween‑20 (PBS‑T).  

3. Block the wells for 1 h at 37 °C using blocking buffer (1.125 % fish‑skin gelatin in PBS‑T).  

4. Add our samples (provided) to the plate in duplicate wells, along with the standard curve (recombinant α‑Syn standards we will supply).  

5. Incubate the plate at room temperature for 2 h.  

6. Add the detection antibody (the “desired antibody” specified in the protocol; we will provide the appropriate antibody) and incubate 1 h at 37 °C.  

7. Wash the plate five times with PBS‑T.  

8. Add ExtrAvidin phosphatase (Sigma, E2636) diluted in the same blocking buffer and incubate 30 min at 37 °C.  

9. Develop color with fast‑p‑nitrophenyl phosphate substrate (Sigma, N1891). Read absorbance at 405 nm every 2.5 min for up to 60 min.  

10. From the kinetic data, identify the time point(s) where both standards and sample dilutions fall on the linear (log‑phase) portion of the curve and report the corresponding concentrations.  

Please let us know if any reagents need to be supplied or if any steps require clarification. Thank you.
